dimensions.assessment: Directly affects members of the Shadow Wolves tactical patrol unit and ICE personnel involved in program administration.
dimensions.evidence: all GS-1801 Tactical Officers who are employed as Shadow Wolves by Homeland Security Investigations

dimensions.assessment: Provides significant employment classification changes and individualized pay and retirement information for qualified agents, but is limited to a specific niche unit.
dimensions.evidence: noncompetitively convert Shadow Wolves, after their successful completion of three years as Shadow Wolves, regardless of location assigned, from the excepted service to career or career conditional appointments in the competitive service.

dimensions.assessment: The bill explicitly states that no additional funds are authorized to be appropriated.
dimensions.evidence: No additional funds are authorized to be appropriated for the purpose of carrying out this Act.

dimensions.assessment: Amends the Homeland Security Act of 2002 and previous enhancement acts to establish specific program requirements, strategies, reporting, and conversion rules.
dimensions.evidence: Subtitle D of title IV of the Homeland Security Act of 2002 (6 U.S.C. 251 et seq.) is amended by adding at the end the following:

dimensions.assessment: Establishes permanent statutory changes regarding conversion eligibility and program structure, alongside one-time reporting requirements.
dimensions.evidence: Not later than 1 year after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Director shall submit a report

missing_information: Exact current headcount of the Shadow Wolves unit affected by the conversion provision.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill provides procedural and workforce enhancements for the Shadow Wolves tactical patrol unit, allowing noncompetitive conversion to the competitive service for eligible agents who have served three years, and directing ICE to update strategies, staffing needs, and succession plans.
